For Kenyan citizens, visa requirements vary by destination and travel purpose, yielding complementary perspectives across the evidence. As of October 2023, Kenyan passport holders had visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 73 countries, ranking 74th globally [d1]. By April 2025, counts showed 46 visa-free destinations, 13 requiring an eVisa, and 140 requiring a pre-travel visa application [d7]. For the United States, Kenyan citizens must obtain an embassy (paper) visa before travel; it is not available online [d2]. U.S. entry also requires a tourist visa for Kenya unless arriving from certain contexts [d3], and Kenya allows tourist visas on arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport as of May 2012 [d4]. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi processes multiple Kenya-related visa categories with reciprocity-based fees and validity periods [d9].

For travel to Schengen countries, Kenyan applicants must submit a Schengen visa application, a passport valid at least three months beyond the stay and issued within the last ten years, passport copies, a national ID copy, a recent photo, travel insurance of at least EUR 30,000, and proof of visa fee payment [d10]. Kenya itself issues several visa types—single journey, transit (≤3 days), diplomatic, courtesy/official, and an East Africa Tourist Visa valid 90 days for multiple entries across Kenya, Rwanda, and Uganda [d6]. General application guidance indicates travelers should apply at the destination country’s embassy or consulate in their country of origin or residence [d5], and Kenyan visa applications require photos, residence/work permit copies, a court decision copy, and an application letter [d8].
